bay_bayou.subject: Executive Summary - Bay Bayou Q2 Six Months Ended June 30, 2026 Financial Statements and Reporting Package
bay_bayou.summary_text:
Bay Bayou RV Resort - Financial Summary for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
Attached Financial Documents:

1.  Comparative Balance Sheet and Income Statement as of June 30, 2026.
  2.  Q2 Year-to-Date and Monthly Operating Statement for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  3.  Monthly Occupancy Report for thru June 2026.
  4.  Monthly ADR (Average Daily Rate) and RevPAR (Revenue per Site) through June 30, 2026.
  5.  Net Cash Flow Statement for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  6.  Detailed Schedule of Capital Additions for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  7.  Rent Roll as of June 30, 2026.

________________________________
The synopsis for the year to date second quarter of 2026 Bay Bayou financial results is slightly lower operating earnings due to lower occupancy, but slightly mitigated by lower operating expenses. Total revenues and NOI produced strong cash flow and demonstrated control in operating expenses after having weathered the late effects of hurricane hits impacting 2025 and early 2026. Another area of improvement were in electric costs, impacted by a utility company storm surcharges last year, and the electric recovery ratio has improved significantly. A new metering system is being installed which should result in an even more efficient recovery.
Financial Highlights:
Financial Highlights:

1.  Rental Revenue & Occupancy:
     *   Total revenues for the year to date second quarter 2026 were lower than 2025, down $118,000 or 5.8%. Contributing to revenues was the new credit card charges of $18K.
     *   Occupancy has continued to trend lower, dropped to 32,920 site nights rented, 59% occupancy from 37,360, or 66% in the prior year to date in Q2.
     *   While occupancy was lower and total rental revenue decreased, the ADR (Average Daily Rate), rose by $3.58 from $53.27 in 2025 to $56.85 Q2 2026.
     *   RevPAR (Revenue per Available Site) decreased by $2.12 due to the lower occupancy and lower stay rental rates.
     *   The lower occupancy has impacted the industry and locally due to an inflationary economy, primarily gas prices, as well as health related cancellations reported.
  2.  Electric Revenue & Expenses:
     *   The electric revenue recovery rate increased from 69% to 74%, due to improvements in billing and collections.  Electric utility costs decreased, $2,035 or 1.5% over last year to date, due to a surcharge billed by the utility company last year to recover storm related costs. As reported last quarter, as the year progresses we should see the recovery rate increase and stabilize.
  3.  Operating Expenses:
     *   Total operating expenses decreased $44,000, or 3.8% year-over-year.
     *   Variances on several operating cost line items were reported year to date, with improvements in advertising, credit card costs, cable and internet costs, insurance, lower repairs and maintenance expenses, utility costs as well as management fees which are a function of the lower revenue. These lower costs however were offset by supplies as well as scheduled payroll costs, refuse removal, auto/maintenance expenses and an estimate of real estate taxes,. (see detailed breakdown attached).
  4.  Capital Improvements:
     *   Total capital expenditures for the year to date Q2 2026 amounted to $101,300, primarily the cost of pond stabilization and the new electric metering systems being installed.
     *   Investments also included minor office equipment and equipment costs.
  5.  Net Operating Income (NOI):
     *   NOI decreased $74k, 8.3% compared to Q2 last year to date.
     *   Lower rental revenue offset by slightly lower operating expenses, decreased net profitability.
  6.  Cash Flow:
     *   Cash flow from operations were $875,500 before capex ($101,300) and mortgage debt reduction ($80,600). (an improvement compared to $792K last year to date).

7.      Litigation:

*   The cost of litigation for 2 matters at Bay Bayou have been borne by Jennings under its presumed management responsibilities for the LLC. These matters and their costs to date were as follows:
     *   1. Smartara v. Bay Bayou. This involved the cancellation of the internet service providers contract and claims for unpaid contract service. Legal fees totaled $102,000 and settlement of $200,000 have been paid to date.
     *   2. Galluzo v. Bay Bayou. This case involved a discrimination allegations for denying rental to customers who had a child in violation of the community's senior living status. Legal fees totaled $10,200 and a settlement of $20,000 have been incurred to date.

________________________________
Next Steps:
Darla will provide further commentary on significant variances observed throughout the year. Specifically, I've asked for her insights on the occupancy results. These responses will be forwarded separately as an addendum to this report.
Jim

park_city.subject: Park City Mobile Homes Inc. and Affiliates Interim Q3 2026 Financial Statements Nine Months Ended July 2026
park_city.summary_text:
Attached are the financial statements and comparative reports for the third fiscal quarter ended July 31, 2026 for the Park City group of entities. These materials are provided to give you a clear picture of the performance and financial position of the consolidated operations, which include:
Included in this report:

1.  Comparative Consolidated Financial Statements (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025)
  2.  Consolidating Statements by individual entities:
     *   PC Mobile Homes, Inc.
     *   Park City Sales Corp.
     *   Park City Plaza, Inc. (Note: now part of the Barbara Descendants Trust)
     *   Park City Manufactured Homes, Inc.
  3.  Operating Expense Detail for the Mobile Home Community (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025)
  4.  Fixed Asset Additions Schedule - primarily related to community enhancements
  5.  Sales and Gross Profit Report - highlights from the sales company
  6.  Inventory Schedule - rental and for-sale mobile homes
  7.  Installment Contract Notes Receivable Schedule - notes receivable from mobile home sales
  8.  Occupancy Report - year-end 2025 and Q3 2026 thru July

________________________________
Financial Highlights - Mobile Home Park Operations

*   Total Revenues increased by $349K Year over Year (YoY), from $5.579M to $5.928M
     *   Primary driver: Rental rate increases on continued stable occupancy and higher MH Unit sales.
     *   Revenue from sale of homes was up by $112K
     *   Utility income (incl trash) also rose by $14K, with an increase in total utility expenses of $31K.
     *   Water Expense Recovery Ratio less at 81% (vs. 85% prior year to date). Mid quarter collections are 1 month in arrears which should stabilize comparison at year end.
     *   The new Garage Fee revenue added $46K to total revenues
  *   Operating Expenses remained stable and expense growth controlled relative to revenue:
     *   MH Op Expenses up $213K YoY, 12.8%, from $2.669M to $2.822M, which increase is primarily in management fees to JRI, increased $187K YoY. Excluding management fees, operating expenses increased slightly, $25K, 1.7%, due to:
     *   Payroll costs rose by $32K, due to routine annual payroll adjustments
     *   R&M expenses were down by $3K, due to the timing of significant projects completed last year (e.g., water/sewer repairs, road crack sealing)
     *   Real Estate Taxes reflect lower actual 2025 and estimated 2026 assessments, $49K. (The actual 2025 total RET were $698K, down from 2024 of $708K)
     *   Utility costs were higher, $26K, 8%, on increased usage and rates
     *   All other operating expense line items were consistent with prior YTD.
  *   Capital Improvements totaled $140K YTD, including:
     *   New garage door for the maintenance building
     *   Concrete upgrades for sites and common areas, as well as electric improvements

________________________________
Park City Sales Corp.

*   Two new and three used home sales closed YTD Q3 (vs. two new and two used units YTD Q3 2025), representing meaningful improvement in volume and profitability per unit.
     *   Net profit: $78K
     *   The 2 new homes and 1 used home sale was financed through 3 installment contracts totaling, $189K
     *   Detailed gross profit breakdown is attached
  *   Rental Income from PC Sales Corp. mobile home units increased to $120K, 2.6% (vs. $117K last year to date)
     *   This reflects ongoing rentals of mobile home units
     *   Lot rental revenue continues to flow to the MHP entity

________________________________
Gain on Sale and Partnership Income

*   Included in Partnership Income is the distribution to the corporation of its share, 25%, of the proceeds from the sale in late May of the Upriver Resort, of $8.4 Mil. A final distribution of minor residual amounts to close the partnership are forthcoming. A tax provision has been estimated on the income.
  *   In addition, recognized partnership income YTD: $1.001M, from the following:
     *   Upriver Partnership: $450K (distributions of 2025 + partial 2026 earnings)
     *   Lakeview Partnership (45% share): $519K
     *   Veranda Six Partnership (50% share): $32K
     *   Note: Poinsettia Partnership (60% share) will report earnings in future periods

________________________________
Capital Resources

*   PC Line of Credit Increased
     *   Effective March 2025, the credit facility expanded from $10.0M to $15.0M
     *   The outstanding balance increased $2 mil in November from $4.1 mil to $6.1 mil to partially fund equity in the recently acquired Manistee MI RV/MH community.
     *   Funds are earmarked for strategic acquisitions, capital improvements, and maintaining a contingency reserve

________________________________
Summary & Outlook
The third quarter reflects healthy top-line growth and operating stability, as well as the partnership income on the sale of its long term investment in Upriver, with positive indicators across revenue, recovery ratios, and other partnership investments. Strategic positioning through our credit line expansion and conservative capital improvements has the corporation well-prepared for upcoming opportunities and potential market shifts.
Please don't hesitate to reach out if you'd like to discuss the details further. I'm happy to walk through any specific item or provide additional insights.
Jim

Enclosed are the financial statements for Sunkissed Village RV Resort LLC for the six months ended June 30, 2026. These statements reflect the financial activity of the partnership and include:

1.  Comparative Balance Sheet (as of June 30, 2026 & 2025)
  2.  Comparative Income Statement & Operating Expense Detail (for the six months ended June 30, 2026 & 2025)
  3.  Monthly Net Operating Income & Net Income Statement (with comparative expense details)
  4.  Statement of Cash Flows (for the six months ended June 30, 2026)
  5.  Rent Roll (as of June 30, 2026)

  7.  Fixed Asset Additions Detail (for the six months ended June 30, 2026)
  8.  Park Model Sales & Inventory Report (as of June 30, 2026)
Financial Performance Overview
Sunkissed Village experienced 3%, $34K, revenue growth compared to last year to date, and, decreased its operating expenses compared to last YTD 2%, $15K. That was primarily due to getting the credit card cost down to a market rate.

*   Total Revenue: $1.249M (vs. $1.215M in 2025). Strong growth on occupancy and rate management.
  *   Net Operating Income (NOI): $506K (vs. $458K in 2025), a 10.5% increase.
  *   Occupancy Rate: Averaged 69% YTD (effectively, 100% occupied at the end of March)
  *   Operating Expenses: $743K, with:

*   Significantly lower costs in credit card charges, reducing the rate from 7+% to 2%.
     *   9% increase in total payrolls, consistent with the full occupancy during the peak season and annual increases.
     *   Utility costs were 7% , higher due to seasonal rate increases. The electric recovery ratio was 90% in Q2 YTD 2026, compared to 100% YTD last year. While the recovery ratio is positive, several factor impact that recovery. 1. Short term stays are not recoverable and there are a higher amount of shorter term stays compared to last year. 2. Guests are billed in arrears which may result in some month to month variance, however annually should have no impact. Water leaks were identified and repaired, contributing to the increase water expense. Electric expense was slightly higher, 4%. This was impacted by higher billing rates and lower seasonal credits applied by the utility.
     *   R & M was slightly higher, $4K, comparative to last year to date.
Key Financial Highlights

1.  Park Model Sales & Inventory- There was no activity in the first and second quarters of 2026 since last year end.
     *   2 new Park Models were delivered and closed in 2025.
     *   As of June 30, 2026, 41 out of 42 new Park Model sites were sold.
     *   1 Park Model remains in inventory, with no additional orders planned.
  2.  Cash Flow & Distributions
     *   Operating cash flow for the year to date was positive at $487K, up from last year to date $458K, reflective of the peak performing seasonal months.
     *   Fixed asset additions totaled $28K, covering additions to FF&E, a water leak repair and other miscellaneous enhancements.
     *   Last years refinanced mortgage loan reduced interest expense significantly compared to last year to date, which contributed to the year to date cash position increase of $349K.
Conclusion
Consistent with the higher occupancy in the first quarter of the year and stable Q2 operating results, revenue and NOI increased, and improvements made in cost controls resulting in strong financial performance. The refinancing of the mortgage loan strengthened our financial position for future growth.
If you have any questions, please reach out.
I will continue to send these reports to Darla for her comments.

Jim

tax_buyers.summary_text:
Executive Summary - Q2 2026 Financial Results
Tax Certificate Buying Entities
Attached are the financial statements and supporting schedules for the six months ended June 30, 2026.The second quarter year to date reflects the returns expected from the increased volume of certificate purchases over the past 2 years, and shows reduced interest expense due to the reduction in bank debt from the utilization of internal working capital.
Key Highlights:

*   Revenue Growth: Total revenue was slightly lower comparable to YTD Q2 2025, but continued to be driven by higher certificate interest income and lower operating cost reimbursements. The reduction reflects the lower certificate volumes purchased last year in the collar 2025 fall sales and delayed Cook sale.
     *   Certificate Interest: $1.525M (down from $1.676M last year)
     *   Reimbursements from Galaxy Sites: $612K (down from $652K). This is the planned management of the operating cost reimbursement fees to control the expense and debt on Galaxy Sites.
  *   Operating Income: $1.519M, lower than last year's $1.685M, impacted by the decreased revenue and mitigated slightly by the control of operating cost expenses which were lower $24K.
  *   Net Income: $813K, up from $727K last year, on lower interest expenses.
     *   Interest Expense: $827K (down from $1.023M last YTD), due to lower bank debt from higher utilization of in house capital.
     *   Interest Income: Higher than last year, as excess cash was borrowed to Point earning the AFR interest rate.
  *   Inventory Position: Ending inventory was $25.8M, lower than $32.8M Year over Year, reflecting lower collar county purchases last fall and the delay in the Cook County sale.
     *   $5.5M from Cook County (Jan & Dec 2024)
     *   $13.5 M collar purchases (Fall 2025) vs. $20M from collar counties (Fall 2024)
  *   Operating Expenses: Decreased to $618K (from $642K), primarily due to lower management fee allocations.
Outlook:
Lower inventory levels will reduce certificate earnings. This has been mitigated by improving certificate yields and utilization of internal borrowing which have provided stable operating performance year to date. The outlook for future earnings will be dependent on certificate purchases from participation in the upcoming fall county tax sales and the tax business as a whole which will become clearer as legislation becomes implemented and strategic goals are redefined based on the new industry environment.
Please reach out with any questions.
Jim

the_bluffs.summary_text:
The Bluffs property, comprised of the mobile home and RV sections, located in Manistee, Michigan, was acquired on November 14, 2025. This summary presents its financial results for the second quarter of 2026.
The attached reports include:

1.  Combining Balance Sheet, Statement of Income and Earnings and Operating Expense Detail. These statements combine the operations of the MH/RV Resort, the Sales entity created to sell MH units, L Sites LLC and the separate expansion land area to be developed, M Sites LLC.
  2.  Statement of Cash Flows for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  3.  Schedule of Fixed Asset Additions Q2.
  4.  Schedule of Sales of Mobile Home Units for the quarters ended June 30, 2026.
  5.  MH Rent Roll as of June 30, 2026, at 100% occupancy, and the RV Rent Roll, at 57% occupancy.

The Bluffs delivered a positive operating profit for the six months ended June 30th, which was enhanced by the profit on the sale of its sole mobile home unit in inventory. The financial activity for the 6 months, however limited, reflect the continuing operations of the MH/RV Resort.
The following highlights the first quarter operating results.
Financial Performance Highlights:

1.  Total Revenue: $,523,400
     *   Mobile home rents: $147,200 (28%)
     *   RV Site rents: Seasonal $101,200 (19%)
     *   Sale of 1 Mobile Home Unit: $241,700 (46%)
Operating Income

1.  Total Operating income for the MH/RV Resort was positive, $139,200, of which $113K from the MH/RV operations, and $26K from the sale of the mobile home unit.. The operations were impacted by startup operating costs, and set up costs. Payroll expenses reflect the sole initial staffing of the On Site Manager, Barry, with stable operations.  Rents were increased January 1, 2026, which rents are reflected in the updated Q2 MH Rent Roll.
  2.  One mobile home unit. At 816 Tennessee, was sold in May at a gross profit of $36,500. Subsequent to this sale, 3 additional units were brokered for sale in June, July and September, which commissions earned will be reported on in Q3.
Operating Expenses:

1.  Total Combined Operating Expenses: ~$179,100
     *   Major Expense Categories:
        *   Salaries & Wages, 25% of operating expense.
        *   Utilities, 10%,  (Electric, Water, Gas) A utilities breakdown is included in the attached. Q2 to date recovery of water and sewer was 64%.
        *   Snow removal (6%) was a significant (seasonal) year to date operating expense, $18K.
        *   Repairs, Supplies, and Maintenance, 2.%.
        *   Professional Fees, 7% - primarily Michigan counsel lease occupancy and review of operating and occupancy agreements, $8,300, plus year-end tax and independent accountants review report cost, $5,200.
Loans and Interest Expense
Interest expense is reflective of the mortgage loan provided by Byline Bank, in the total amount of $2,950,000. $2,200,000 attributable to the MH/RV Resort, $750,000 attributed to the expansion parcel of land. The $2,2 Mil note is a 7 year term, at the 7 year treasury rate +250bps. The land loan has a 1 year term, renewable, interest only at the same rate. These rates approximated at 6.15% in May. The Land loan is planned to be paid off at its maturity in November, 2026.

Cash flow is reflected in the attached statement for the six months ended. $26K was used for operating activities, $275K invested in capital improvements, $44K in loan principle payments, therefore $355K was contributed by the members in capital.

Assets, Liabilities and Capital

1.  A cost segregation report was commissioned and it's results reflected on the Balance Sheet with the goal to maximize taxable depreciation costs of all assets acquired.
  2.  The combined operations were capitalized in accord with the LLC deal structure, with subsequent funding of capital needs financed by K Sites LLC, one of its members.
  3.  Subsequent to the purchase of the assets, fixed asset Additions for the quarter totaled $81k, detailed in the attached. These included pre land development engineering and construction management consultant fees, as well as addition of a garage and electrical hookup to the mobile home inventory unit.

Expansion Plan

A development team has been assembled and the development plans are being executed for the expansion of the site. More details to follow.

Jim

  *   Operating Income (after management fees): ($337,300)

This investment is included on the balance sheet as Investment in Real Estate at cost. As of June 30, 2026, the project was 85% complete and the NAV of this investment was $14 Mil. An Asset Report as of Q2 2026 is attached.
________________________________
Closing Remarks
Please refer to the attached documents for further detail on each item summarized above. Should you have any questions or require clarification, let me know.
________________________________
